# Secondary-axis supplied location transforms

`secondary_transform_reference.json` is generated by executing the complete
fixed Matplotlib 3.11.2 `SecondaryAxis` class and original transform, blend
factory, locator, and Bbox implementations. The generated Scene whitebox tests
compare the supported immutable native-affine profile with those source results.

The reference generator is independent of the Moon implementation. It reuses
`generate_secondary_lifecycle_reference.load_secondary_source` for a consistent
original class identity and pinned dependency checks. It does not import an
installed Matplotlib package or depend on ignored preparation artifacts.

## Reproduce

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/lampese/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 scripts/generate_secondary_transform_reference.py
/Users/lampese/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 scripts/generate_secondary_transform_reference.py --check
```

The optional positional argument is the pinned `lib/matplotlib/ticker.py` path.
The fixed source hash checks also cover the original secondary, transform, Axis,
scale, API, rc, and graphical numeric-host dependencies recorded in the JSON.
Generation formats only its generated Moon file through `moonfmt -`; this is
neither a Moon compile check nor a behavioral acceptance gate.

Reference runtime: CPython 3.12.14 and NumPy 2.3.5, Darwin arm64.
The JSON SHA-256 is
`7de21b7671d83df4b7a4216350c44781325c14096b25dd04a8f2b123ec888e5e`.

## Counts and projection

There are 52 original-source records. The first 34 preparation records are
preserved in their entirety, with no altered state fields or numeric values.
Eighteen additional records exercise deferred placement after failed setters
and nonfinite native-affine input. Thirty-eight private scenario functions run
in two registered test groups, containing at most 32 functions each.

| Original profile | Records | Typed scenarios |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| x/y constructors, ten transform classes/profiles each | 20 | 14 |
| Failing rotation setter | 2 | 2 |
| Omitted and explicit None reset traces | 2 | 2 |
| Original mutable-transform aliases | 2 | 0 |
| Forward-callback capture traces | 4 | 2 |
| Bbox primitive comparisons | 4 | 0 |
| Failed setter followed by positioned aspect | 2 | 2 |
| Selected diagonal/translation NaN and infinities | 12 | 12 |
| NaN in either off-diagonal followed by aspect | 4 | 4 |
| Total | 52 | 38 |

Fourteen source-only records remain visible in the JSON: six generic/wrapper/base
Transform constructors, two direct mutable-alias traces, two callback traces
that mutate the old transform object in place, and four Bbox primitive records.
These are not counted as migrated API parity scenarios.

## Supported native-affine behavior

The supplied transform is an existing immutable `Affine2D` value, corresponding
to the original direct `Affine2DBase` blend path. Secondary x uses the supplied
y component and parent-relative x component; secondary y uses supplied x and
parent-relative y. A supplied identity therefore differs from None, which uses
the parent's transform for both coordinates.

Both off-diagonal coefficients participate in the original whole-transform
separability check. Rotation/skew and NaN in either off-diagonal are rejected,
including an off-diagonal not selected by the child's orientation. Negative
scale, zero scale, NaN/Inf diagonal, and NaN/Inf translation are accepted. There
is no supplied inverse request or finite/positive-scale validation in this path.

Setter order matters. After a valid location is assigned, a failing blend keeps
the new requested location but leaves the old installed locator unchanged.
The reference checks the new metadata, unchanged installed position/transform,
and a later positioned aspect operation still using that old locator. A
wrong-orientation location instead fails before metadata is assigned.

Omitting transform in a later `set_location` clears a prior transform. Explicit
None does the same; omission has no keep-old-transform interpretation. Updating
location does not eagerly change active geometry, own view, or alignment.

The current positioned operation captures the old installed locator before the
forward callback maps limits. A callback may install a new position and affine
value, but the current placement still uses the captured old locator. The new
snapshot is for the next placement. The reference asserts both current geometry
and the newly installed snapshot rather than reading latest metadata twice.

## Native graph and Bbox boundaries

Original `blended_transform_factory` uses native class provenance. A direct
rotated Affine2D is rejected, while a rotated CompositeGenericTransform or
TransformWrapper takes the generic blend path and is accepted. Even original
base Transform(), with `has_inverse=False`, is accepted by this placement path.
Those observations do not broaden the immutable-affine API into arbitrary
Transform protocols or convert every affine tree into the direct-native class.

Original mutable transforms remain aliased through their graph. A lazy candidate
can observe mutation of the old transform during a forward callback; an already
copied active bbox does not move until aspect applies again. The immutable Moon
value profile preserves replacement-only capture and explicitly excludes native
in-place mutable transform aliases.

The source Bbox comparison records distinguish two different original methods.
`BboxBase.transformed` transforms three selected points. `TransformedBbox` uses
all four corners and restores raw inversion after reduction. The global Moon
BBox helper is not claimed as a complete clone of both. The tested placement
profile uses the original thin positive-width/height requested rectangle.

## Host, errors, and numerical assertions

The common host uses figure size 320x240, parent normalized rectangle
`[.2,.25,.5,.5]`, x-view `[1,4]`, y-view `[10,20]`, and actual source parent frame
`[64,60,160,120]`. Original numeric constructor, Axis/function-scale, deferred
locator, aspect, and Bbox methods execute. Graphical constructor/style sinks are
inherited from the accepted lifecycle loader. This is not full GUI, artist
rendering, or arbitrary callback-vector protocol parity.

Finite values and infinities are compared by binary64 bits; NaN is compared by
classification, without a NaN payload promise. Original native nonfinite affine
composition propagates the selected NaN/Inf inputs into four NaN bbox quantities.
Those source results are checked without requiring complete SVG export.

Exact native exception type/message remains in JSON. Moon assertions use the
existing checked Core `InvalidTicks` mapping and verify surviving state; they
do not establish a new verbatim exception-message contract. Original transform
identity fields remain source observations; the immutable bridge asserts its
installed position and six affine coefficients directly.

Root's unified acceptance passed after all tracked writers stopped. Initial
`moon check --target all` passed with zero errors and seven existing Ref warnings;
`moon info && moon fmt` passed. All 41 interfaces were reviewed: only Scene and
pyplot add the optional affine parameter/import, while the other 39 are unchanged.

`moon test --target all` passed completely: wasm, wasm-gc and native each
22038/22038, JavaScript 22045/22045. The 16 new registered tests are these two
formal groups, seven Scene state/geometry hands and seven Scene/pyplot rendering
hands. Root independently compared all original 34 records exactly, and a separate
read-only review checked every formal scenario's reachability and stage projection.
The final source `--check` and static/interface gates are recorded in the migration
checkpoint; no old source JSON expected value was edited.
